slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Onsoo enter the US market in 2027, and if so by which route, within an $18M cash cap, payback by 2030 and an 8% group margin floor?
Is the US market large and growing enough, and where do K-beauty buyers shop?
Does the Amazon pilot show that Onsoo can win and keep US customers?
Which route, Amazon-led or retail-led, gives Onsoo the better start?
Does the route fit the board's cash, payback and margin limits, and beat a Japan scale-up?
How should Onsoo launch, and what would make it slow down or change course?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO Park Ji-won with the board: approve or reject US entry and choose the route

Peak cumulative US cash need of no more than $18M through 2030; Cumulative US cash back to zero by the end of 2030; Group operating margin at or above 8% in every year; A US business on the way to the $40M revenue ambition; Only one major new-market launch in 2027
Board meeting, March 2027
Mass retail and brand-website (DTC) routes: no planning inputs; Markets other than the US and Japan; Currency hedging

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not retail, and hold ad cost near the pilot's 28%
The US is worth entering: Onsoo's segment is a $3.6B market growing fast
–	K-beauty took 39% of US facial skincare growth in 2021–25; Amazon carries 41% of its sales
The Amazon pilot proves demand, but repeat purchase trails US newcomers
–	Monthly units nearly doubled in six months, but 90-day repeat is 29%, against 31%
Amazon beats retail: at Onsoo's awareness, doors would sell below the removal line
–	Low-awareness brands sell 2.6 units per door a week, against 4.0 required
Option A is the only US route within the limits, but reaches about $26M by 2030, not $40M
–	Option B breaks the $18M cap and the 8% floor; Japan earns more cash but stays small
–	Option A pays back by 2030 only below 28.6% average ad cost
Launch in mid-2027 under five gates, and defer retail until awareness passes 20%
–	Ad cost, the tariff and 2027 volume decide whether to slow down
–	Size cash on the $3.9M stress-case peak and set the 2030 goal at $26M

slides.title: BACKUP: Per unit, retail earns more than Amazon, but it carries a fixed cost that Amazon avoids

paragraphs.text: 1 Market    2 Right to win    3 Route    4 Economics    5 Plan
BACKUP: Per unit, retail earns more than Amazon, but it carries a fixed cost that Amazon avoids
Rice Ferment Barrier Cream, contribution per unit by channel, $ per unit, 15% duty
Retail's unit margin does not survive its fixed cost
▪	Retail fixed cost: $7.5M a year for national marketing and field sales, on top of Option A's $2.1M
▪	Amazon: advertising is variable, so spend can be cut the quarter ad cost runs high
▪	Duty: a rise to 25% adds $0.35 a unit in either channel
1  Planning-team Table 4 and Table 6; wholesale is 50% of the $28.00 shelf price
Sources: Planning-team unit economics, hero cream (briefing pack §7); Amazon US pilot, Jan–Jun 2026 (briefing pack §6); team analysis

BACKUP: On evidence-based sell-through and no halo, Option B's cash need would pass Mooncrest's loss by 2030
Option B model on evidence inputs, median sell-through for brands below 10% awareness, no Amazon halo, team estimate
Closer to Mooncrest than to the plan
▪	Sell-through: 2.6 units per door a week, the median for Onsoo's awareness band
▪	Removal risk: below the 4.0 line, the doors would likely be lost after the 12-month review
▪	Mooncrest: lost an estimated $21M after a 450-door retail-first entry
1  Doors and costs as in Option B; Amazon volumes as in Option A at the pilot's 28% ad cost
Sources: Planning-team forecasts and US costs (briefing pack §8); Retail analytics firm, 2025, newcomer brands in US specialty retail (briefing pack §9); team analysis

BACKUP: The Japan scale-up adds $7.0M of revenue by 2030 and $1.8M of cumulative cash
Option J model, planning-team Japan case, team estimate
Safe, but capped by its market
▪	Margin: 30% contribution less $0.8M fixed cost a year and $1.0M one-time
▪	Market: Japan facial skincare grows about 1.5% a year, and Onsoo already holds 3.1%
▪	No working capital: the Japan case carries none, which flatters its cash against Option A
1  Planning-team Table 7; cash taken as equal to operating result
Sources: Planning-team Japan scale-up case (briefing pack §8); team analysis
